brief: Hungary's professional-interpreter layer for banking and payments regulation splits cleanly into three tiers: Big Four regulatory desks (KPMG Hungary's Financial Risk & Regulation monthly digest is the standout, with a live Hungarian-language blog behind it; Deloitte Legal and PwC/Réti Várszegi follow, and EY is a confirmed blank), international law firms publishing dated English alerts on Hungarian instruments (CMS, Wolf Theiss, Schoenherr, Kinstellar, DLA Piper — Schoenherr and CMS notably covering MNB soft law and DORA scoping before official English texts), and Hungarian-first boutiques of which Gárdos Mosonyi Tomori is the deepest on pénzforgalom and MNB decrees. The fastest route to the whole universe is the pointer layer: fetching Mondaq's Hungary finance-and-banking hub directly enumerated active Hungarian contributors, and Legal 500/Chambers rankings give the full ranked firm list for a per-firm site sweep. Collection should key every interpreter alert to the primary instrument on mnb.hu or Net Jogtár, since the interpreters' value is the date-stamping and translation, not the underlying obligation.
